blurb: Device passcodes are the foundation of iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS data security. A user's passcode is combined with the device's hardware UID using PBKDF2-AES tangling performed exclusively in the Secure Enclave, producing a passcode-derived key (PDK) that wraps Data Protection class keys. This tangling ensures brute-force attacks must occur on the specific device, subject to mandatory hardware-enforced delays between attempts that escalate from milliseconds to hours. The secure nonvolatile storage component provides anti-replay protection, preventing backup-and-restore techniques from defeating attempt counters. Devices can be configured to erase after ten failed attempts.
